While HGV infection has been observed in patients with cryptogenic liver disease, particularly in Southern Italy, its frequency does not surpass that of hepatitis C virus (HCV) infections.

TT virus, on the other hand, is extremely uncommon among patients with cryptogenic or HCV-related liver disease who do not have a history of parenteral exposure. The current evidence suggests that TT virus infection plays no role in the etiology of cryptogenic chronic liver disease.

"In Southern Italy, hepatitis G virus infection is widespread among patients with chronic hepatitis, independently of parenteral risk factors. Its frequency in subjects with cryptogenic liver disease parallels that observed in HCV chronic liver disease, thus ruling out an aetiologic role of hepatitis G virus. TT virus infection is uncommon in patients with cryptogenic or HCV-related liver disease who do not have a history of parenteral exposure."
